## I1
One-Sentence Story: For interrupted robot programs with commuting actions, a bounded-width partial-order memory can preserve exactly the information required for safe continuation while using less memory than a serialized event log.
Theme: Efficiency and Systems
Form: new mechanism or new problem
Summary: Store executed action dependencies as a frontier, together with confirmed and pending outcomes. Two action prefixes may be merged only when their continuation languages coincide under the supplied task dependency graph. The setting forces treatment of pending outcomes and noncommuting contacts together: a simple bag of events loses dependencies, and ordinary FIFO compression discards pending outcomes. The claimed contribution is an output-sensitive frontier update and a sufficient condition for safe merging, not the general proposition that partial orders compress traces. At width w, the proposed state uses O(w log n) event identifiers; the theorem obligation is continuation equivalence under the specified dependency and feedback assumptions. No experiment has been run; no measured gain is claimed.
Minimal Falsification Experiment: First enumerate all prefixes in six dependency graphs with 6–12 actions and compare all enabled continuations against the exact serialized-state oracle. Any false-safe continuation kills the sufficient-condition claim. Then run 1,200 paired interruption seeds across 30 unseen manipulation graphs, three training seeds, and two delay levels. Compare the method with E3's strongest learned trace compressor and E4's strongest executable belief tracker, both selected by held-out validation, plus exact full-log and no-memory references. Use identical frozen perception/control, 8,000 training trajectories, a 128-token memory budget, equal observation/compute budgets, and the same action horizon. Ablate pending-outcome tracking and partial-order merging independently. Two researchers, two A100 GPUs, 48 GPU-hours plus CPU enumeration suffice for the first paper. Primary metric is unsafe-continuation episodes/all interrupted episodes, with completion rate and memory bytes jointly reported. The hypothesized benefit is a Pareto improvement in memory/error, not a preclaimed number. Kill the mechanism if it violates continuation equivalence, or if its 95% paired interval excludes an improvement of at least 5 percentage points in unsafe continuations at matched completion relative to the strongest budget-matched baseline.
Why It May Be Novel: E1 establishes trace compression only for completed, synchronous operations; E2 establishes delayed-belief tracking without action-dependency compression. E5 supplies a concrete case requiring their interaction. A new frontier rule must establish continuation equivalence and outperform both E3 and E4 at fixed memory.
